note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old man with new-onset, mildly warm, non-painful swelling of the left elbow for one week, without trauma, concerning for olecranon bursitis; further workup for inflammatory, infectious, and metabolic etiologies planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling at the left elbow, noticed approximately one week ago.
- Timeline: Onset about one week ago; persistent since onset; patient reports the swelling feels slightly better at time of consult.
- Characteristics: Swelling is mildly warm, non-painful, with possible fluid sensation; mild discomfort adjacent to swelling but able to move elbow normally; no redness reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.
- Associated symptoms: No systemic symptoms (no fever or acute illness); skin at tip of elbow noted as somewhat dry; no other areas of dry skin; no limitation of movement; no history of similar episodes.
- Pertinent negatives: Denies trauma; denies significant physical activity or occupational strain; denies tenderness on tip of elbow; no personal or clear family history of rheumatologic disease (see family history).

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis, diagnosed by GP several years ago, sometimes with joint pain (no specific complications noted).
- No other significant medical conditions reported.

Medications:
- No current regular medications.
- Ibuprofen recommended (400mg twice daily after food; dose/route/frequency documented).
- Allergies: Peanut allergy; no known medication allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk job (not physically demanding).
- Activity: Runs regularly (2–3 times per week).
- Lifestyle: Normally fit and active; mobile.
- Smoking/alcohol/substance use: Not mentioned.

Family History:
- No known family history of rheumatologic diseases (patient unsure but does not recall any relevant conditions in family).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Exam findings via video:
    - Mild swelling at left elbow (olecranon region).
    - Slight warmth to touch versus adjacent skin.
    - Mild discomfort adjacent to swelling on palpation; not tender at tip.
    - No evident redness.
    - Full range of motion.
    - Skin at tip of elbow slightly dry.
    - No other significant findings reported.

Investigations:
- Planned: Blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and gout (no results available at this time).
- No imaging ordered or mentioned.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
    - Most likely left olecranon bursitis (likely non-infectious), with planned workup to rule out infection and metabolic/rheumatic causes.
- DDx Integration (brief):
    - Olecranon bursitis (non-infectious): Most likely; fits history of swelling, warmth, lack of trauma, absence of significant pain, redness, or systemic symptoms.
    - Septic olecranon bursitis (infectious): Less likely as patient is well, without redness, severe pain, or systemic features, but mild warmth warrants exclusion.
    - Gout: Possible given age and monoarticular swelling, but lack of severe pain and no prior gout diagnosis are against.
- Issue 1: Left elbow swelling (suspected olecranon bursitis)
    - Assessment: Typical for olecranon bursitis, mild warmth/discomfort, no trauma/systemic illness.
    - Plan:
        - Advise regular ibuprofen 400mg twice daily after food.
        - Arrange blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, uric acid for gout).
        - Safety net advice: Advise urgent reconsultation if elbow becomes very red, more painful, redness spreads, or if systemic symptoms develop (to rule out septic arthritis).
        - Review blood test results; arrange follow-up (remote or in-person as patient preference) after tests.
- Issue 2: Osteoarthritis (background)
    - Assessment: Known diagnosis; not currently symptomatic, does not explain current presentation.
    - Plan: None at present.
- Issue 3: Peanut allergy
    - Assessment: Not relevant to presenting complaint but documented for safety.
    - Plan: Continue peanut avoidance; no intervention needed here.
- General plan items:
    - Arrange follow-up after blood tests to review clinical and investigational findings.
    - Patient to seek urgent care if any clinical deterioration as per safety netting.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals, smoking/alcohol/substance use, medication reconciliation/update; occupational history partially addressed.
● No identified conflicts between transcript and DDx.
● Transcript quality: Comprehensible, minor omissions/redactions, generally adequate for clinical documentation.
